description: Eroded world from a seed (eroded-world recipe): the terrain stages, a coarse climate (32 columns, 2 coupling iterations), fluvial erosion (stream power law with deposition and hillslope diffusion, routing itself) and the fjords, the full climate on the eroded terrain, then the flow routing and the hydrology (rivers and lake levels). Judged by the user's review; checks guard the sediment budget, drainage, discharge monotonicity and value ranges. The land-mean denudation rate and the lake count are reported numbers, not checks; Earth hypsometry is context for the review, not a target.

maps.name: erosion-rate
maps.title: Erosion rate (log10 m/Myr, mean over the erosion run; dark where there is none)

maps.name: deposition-rate
maps.title: Deposition rate (log10 m/Myr; dark where there is none)

maps.name: discharge
maps.title: Discharge (log10 m3/s; dark where there is none)

maps.name: sediment-flux
maps.title: Sediment flux a land cell passes to its receiver (log10 thousand m3/yr, mean over the erosion run; the legend's m3/s are thousand m3/yr; dark where there is none)

maps.name: lake-depth
maps.title: Lake depth: filled surface above the terrain (m; dark outside depressions)

maps.name: depressions
maps.title: Depressions (id folded onto 12 colours; dark outside depressions)

maps.name: basins
maps.title: Drainage basins (outlet folded onto 12 colours; dark at sea)

maps.name: river-flow
maps.title: River flow in January (legacy flow units)

maps.name: lakes
maps.title: Lake surface elevation (m above sea level; dark where there is no lake)

review_status: Draft written by an agent on 2026-10-06 (erosion plan, step A3). The user rewrites it; until then a verdict on it is a reading aid, not a judgement of the world.

review.question: Does every river reach the sea or a lake?
review.good: connected courses that gain discharge downstream and end at a coast or a lake; no river that stops on dry land or crosses a range

review.question: Do the largest rivers drain the wettest highlands?
review.good: the highest discharges downstream of wet uplands; dry regions with small rivers except those fed from wet highlands

review.question: Do valleys widen downstream and do plains aggrade?
review.good: erosion concentrated in steep headwaters and along trunk valleys that widen downstream; deposition on lowland plains, basins and at river mouths

review.question: Are the ranges kept, and is the eroded terrain free of grid patterns?
review.good: every range of the tectonic relief still stands, dissected by valleys; no stripes along rows or columns, no diagonal or blocky drainage, no seams at the date line or the poles
